ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 3636, as last amended by Act No. 20054, effective 2024); Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using of Certain Financial Transaction Information; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU); Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 289-300 regarding incorporation and shares; Specific Financial Transactions Information Act (for AML/CFT obligations of financial companies); Regulations on the Reporting and Review of Beneficial Owner Information under the Act on Registration of Real Rights over Real Estate (for parallel UBO concepts in real property, where applicable); and the Framework Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Korea's national AML/CFT framework).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Registration Certificate, 사업자등록증 equivalent for corporation registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce (Court Registration Office, Supreme Court of Korea)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by Korean Court Registry; notarized by a Korean notary public; then authenticated by the Apostille Section of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (Hague Apostille). For non-Hague countries, consular legalization at the embassy/consulate of the destination country in Korea; for Korean documents destined for countries that are not parties to the Apostille Convention, the same European/Asian route requires MOFA authentication followed by destination-country consular legalization. Never chain Hague Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Recent Corporate Registration Extract, 법인등기사항증명서)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registration Office (Daejeon District Court, or local branch having jurisdiction over the registered office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Court-issued extract; notarized by Korean notary; then submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Apostille Section) for Hague Apostille if the destination state is an Apostille Convention member. If destination is a non-member state, MOFA authentication followed by consular legalization at the destination country's diplomatic mission in Korea. The two authentication mechanisms are parallel alternatives; no sequential chaining of Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney for incorporation and foreign filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa board of directors (to be adopted at a shareholders/board meeting, certified by the incorporator or foreign counsel)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Corporate resolution executed in Korea; notarized before a Korean notary public; apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the receiving jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille member. For non-member jurisdictions, notarization followed by MOFA authentication and then consular legalization at the relevant embassy/consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never used in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators / Korean licensed legal professional (certified as per Commercial Act, Article 292)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed articles of association; notarized by Korean notary; then Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for member states; for non-member states, consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate after MOFA authentication. Both paths remain parallel alternatives and are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (from a Korean financial institution verifying the company's banking relationship and anticipated UBO identification status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank in Korea where the corporate account has been provisionally opened or where promoters hold a pre-incorporation currency account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-issued on bank letterhead; notarized by a Korean notary public; authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs with a Hague Apostille for qualified recipient states. For non-Apostille states, bank letter is notarized, then submitted for MOFA authentication and final consular legalization at the destination country's consulate in Korea. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; no sequential application.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Investor Registration Certificate or Certificate of Foreign Exchange Transactions (if any foreign direct investment or BOP reporting is required)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certificate issued by Korean authorities; notarized as needed; for Apostille countries, certified by Korea's MOFA Apostille section; for non-Apostille countries, consular legalization by the destination state's embassy in Korea after MOFA authentication. Apostille and consular legalization are separate, non-combinable authentication tracks.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to incorporation and throughout the client lifecycle, the law firm and the Korean financial institution must conduct mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Korean Ministry of Strategy and Finance consolidated sanctions list, and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit's advisory notices. Screening must include a perpetual negative news search and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database check applying a risk-based approach, with enhanced due diligence triggered for any PEP, family member, or close associate, including source of wealth and source of funds verification. All hits must be documented, escalated, and if confirmed, the matter must be rejected or subjected to internal escalation and a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU. These protocols must be applied in real time during the formation phase, with periodic re-screening at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registration Information System (인터넷등기소, i-REG / 인터넷등기소, 'Registration Information System') and the Korean Corporation Name Search / Name Pre-Claim portal operated by the Supreme Court's Court Registration Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean legal entities must adopt a Korean-language corporate name; the name may include Korean words, numerals, and selected Latin or Chinese characters only as permitted by the Commercial Act. For a Chusik Hoesa, the name must include the element '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa) either at the beginning or end of the name. The statute requires a clear distinction from existing domestic entity names; no exact identical name may be registered, and names that are confusingly similar in sound or with a 'same or similar' trade name are subject to refusal. For transliteration, the Korean name is romanized according to the Revised Romanization of Korean system only where an English reference name is needed; however, the official legal name remains the Hangul name. Four-tier naming conventions must be considered: (1) the distinctive element, (2) the business-objectives description, (3) the corporate form-designating component '주식회사', and (4) optional English trade name, with any English name registered as a trade name (상호) but the statutory corporate name in Hangul is controlling for registry and banking purposes. Foreign characters are only allowed in supplementary trade names; the principal trade name registered under the Commercial Act must be in Korean.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: President of the Republic of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is refused by the Court Registration Office, the applicant must first request a written statement of grounds from the registration officer (completion of the administrative review process). Within 14 days after receiving the statement, the applicant may file a written objection to the court of the same district using Form No. 7 (prescribed in the Court Registration Rules), explaining the factual and legal distinction from the conflicting name. Alternatively, the applicant may file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the refusal, asking the competent administrative court to invalidate the refusal. If the refusal was based on similarity to an existing trade name, the applicant should either obtain a written consent from the existing name holder and submit evidence to the registry, or amend the distinctive portion and resubmit. The appeal brief must include the exact rejected name, the registration office's decision reference number, the statutory provisions relied upon, and proof of the applicant's legal interest. If time is of the essence, the applicant may simultaneously file a new name reservation request with a distinct name while pursuing the appeal, but the appeals route does not automatically extend the 30-day reservation window. A lawyer regularly admitted in Korea should prepare the administrative appeal to ensure the registry's naming precedents are accurately addressed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under Korean law, a Chusik Hoesa must have a registered head office within Korea that is determined by the articles of incorporation; the address must be a physically existing place where the company's management functions are actually exercised. A virtual office or commercial mailbox without a lease of physical premises is generally not accepted by the Korean tax authorities (National Tax Service) or domestic banks for the Micro-SaaS industry, especially for obtaining a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) and opening a corporate bank account which requires in-person verification and a physical office visit in certain cases. Although online-only businesses may operate from a home address or serviced office, the National Tax Service expects lease agreements, utility bills, and evidence of actual business substance at the address upon registration and during on-site verification. Pure virtual office arrangements, where no staff is present during business hours and only a mail-forwarding service exists, are rejected by major banks as insufficient for account opening and by the NTS for input tax credit purposes. For a low-risk Micro-SaaS company using payment platforms such as Paddle and Lemon Squeezy, a serviced office with a dedicated room and a management company agreement can be acceptable, provided that the address appears as the company's registered address in the corporate registry and NTS filings, and where the company maintains exclusive access to the space, business signage, books and records, and corporate email.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) The company must maintain original or electronic records of corporate minutes, share register, accounting books, VAT invoices, and employment contracts at the registered office; (2) the registered office must contain evidence of actual management activity such as a desk, computer, business files, and communication equipment; (3) written notices displayed in Korean showing the company's full name and registration number; (4) lease agreement in the company's name covering the exact registered office; (5) a bank confirmation or utility bill addressed to the company; (6) the officers' and directors' contact details are available on site. Unannounced physical on-site inspections by municipal tax officials (NTS) or registration authorities are moderately possible, with quantified risk at about 25% during the first year, especially after VAT re-registration or bank account opening. If the company claims a specific business activity code, NTS has in recent years conducted random targeted inspections of small companies engaged in online software businesses as part of tax post-audit programs. However, for a micro-SaaS company with a low-risk profile, the chance of an unannounced inspection remains below 30% unless the company claims a separate tax-free or e-commerce incentive, applies for state-supported benefits, or shows abnormal transactional patterns through Paddle/Lemon Squeezy.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean corporate registration fee (법인설립등기 신고 수수료 / court registration allowance and 'registration and license tax' for capital not exceeding KRW 100 million)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Government Legislation / Supreme Court Registration Office (court fees) and local municipal government (registration license tax)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Registration License Tax Act and Court Fees Act; fee scales are progressive based on capital amount (approx. KRW 150,000-250,000 for typical micro-cap).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and board resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per Korean notary fee schedule; typically KRW 50,000-100,000 per document depending on page count and number of witnesses.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) Hague Apostille authentication for three originals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Korea (Apostille Section)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of KRW 1,000 to 3,000 per document; estimated at USD 15 for five documents; actual cost may include courier and agency handling fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and registry search official extracts (법인등기부등본, including additional English translation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per certified copy of the current corporate registry; typically KRW 1,000 per extract plus online issuance charges; USD estimate includes three extracts and English notarization of translation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Korean legal counsel fee for preparation of articles of incorporation, shareholder resolution, initial treasury stock compliance, and pre-incorporation due diligence report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a simple Chusik Hoesa formation with one class of shares and no foreign investment threshold; ranges USD 1,500-3,500 depending on complexity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax office business registration certificate (사업자등록증) filing and value-added tax registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - no official fee for bare registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No government fee for tax registration; USD 100 is an allowance for Korean CPA or tax accountant (세무사) filing assistance at prevailing hourly rates.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening assistance and compliance fee (FATCA/CRS/KYC verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean commercial bank (via due diligence/onboarding departments) and assisting local compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank may charge a one-time corporate account opening fee (KRW 100,000-200,000) and the compliance consultant's service charge based on market rate of KRW 200,000-400,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and notarized English certification of statutory documents, including apostille-related courier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean notary public, certified translator, and international courier service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of KRW 3,000-8,000 per Korean character page for certified legal translation; courier fee of USD 40-80.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288-317 (incorporation of stock companies), particularly Articles 289 (articles of incorporation), 295 (subscription of shares), 306 (registration of incorporation), and 317 (effect of registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office (Registration Court) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, under the Supreme Court of Korea
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (주식회사 설립등기신청서) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting documents
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Commercial Act, there is no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the total subscription price must be fully paid in before registration, and the funds must be deposited in a bank account in the name of the company (or a designated trustee account) until registration is completed. The deposit certificate must be submitted to the registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company')

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the Commercial Act of South Korea, and the undersigned directors have been duly appointed by the incorporators;

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to adopt resolutions on matters necessary for the establishment and operation of the Company;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board acknowledges that the total issued and paid-in share capital of the Company is [amount] Korean Won, consisting of [number] shares with a par value of [value] Korean Won each, all of which have been fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The Board ratifies the subscription and payment of the share capital and confirms that the capital has been deposited in the Company's designated bank account as required by law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the opening of a corporate bank account with [Bank Name] and designates the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as the sole authorized signatories for all banking transactions, including deposits, withdrawals, wire transfers, and the execution of any banking agreements. All transactions shall be subject to the Company's internal control policies and shall require dual signatures for amounts exceeding [threshold] Korean Won.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [Full Address], as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease, service, or maintenance agreements necessary for the operation of such office. The registered office shall be the legal seat of the Company for all statutory and administrative purposes.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are duly elected and qualified. The officers are authorized to execute all documents, file all statutory returns, and take all actions necessary to carry out the Company's business, including the procurement of business licenses, tax registrations, and other permits.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the officers to engage legal counsel, accountants, and other professional advisors as necessary to ensure full compliance with Korean corporate law and to represent the Company before any governmental or regulatory authority.

6. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting. The officers are directed to file a copy of these minutes with the Company's statutory records.

Dated this [day] day of [month], [year].

[Signature of Chairperson]
[Signature of Directors]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증사) in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, business purpose, registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and provisions for directors and auditors. The incorporators must sign and seal the articles. The articles must be notarized by a notary public, who will verify the identity and legal capacity of the incorporators. If any incorporator is a legal entity, a certificate of corporate existence and power of attorney must be provided. The notarization process ensures the authenticity of the signatures and the legality of the articles. After notarization, the articles become the foundational document for registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (in Korean)
Identification documents of all incorporators (passport or resident registration card)
Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented
Certificate of seal (if applicable)
Proof of address of the registered office (e.g., lease agreement)
Notarization fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises objections or requests amendments, correct the articles and resubmit. If the notary refuses to notarize due to substantive legal issues, seek legal counsel to revise the articles or consult a different notary. Any delay in notarization will extend the overall timeline; therefore, ensure all information is accurate and complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and Full Payment of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Korea (for deposit) and the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the incorporators must subscribe to all shares. The total subscription price must be paid in full. Payment is made by depositing the amount into a bank account opened in the name of the company (or a designated trustee account). The bank will issue a certificate of deposit confirming the payment. If there are multiple incorporators, each must pay their respective subscription amount. The deposit must be completed before the registration application is filed. The certificate of deposit is a mandatory document for registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit from the bank
Subscription list (if multiple subscribers)
Receipts of payment
Bank account opening documents (if not already opened)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (for bank reference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not completed, the incorporation cannot proceed. If there is a delay, the subscription may be rescinded, and the incorporators may need to restart the process. Ensure that the bank account is opened correctly and that the deposit is made in the exact amount required. If the bank refuses to issue a certificate, resolve any discrepancies with the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Directors and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators (for initial appointment) and the Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must appoint the initial directors and auditors (if required). For a Chusik Hoesa, at least one director is required; if the company has a board of directors, at least three directors are required. The appointment is made by a resolution of the incorporators. After appointment, the directors must convene a first board meeting to adopt the pro-forma resolution covering share capital, banking authorization, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. The meeting must be properly minuted, and all directors must sign the minutes. The minutes serve as evidence of the board's decisions and are required for registration.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the incorporators' meeting (appointing directors)
Minutes of the first board meeting (adopting the resolution)
Consent forms from each director and auditor
Identification documents of directors and auditors
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (for reference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director fails to accept the appointment, replace them with a qualified individual. Ensure all minutes are properly executed and dated. If the board meeting is challenged, reconvene and adopt a corrective resolution. Any errors in the minutes must be corrected before submission to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry Office (Registration Court) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation to the court registry. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of deposit, minutes of the incorporators' meeting and first board meeting, consent forms, and other required documents. The court will review the application for compliance with the Commercial Act. If satisfied, the court will register the company and issue a certificate of registration. The registration fee must be paid at the time of submission. After registration, the company is legally incorporated and may commence business.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation (form)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of deposit
Minutes of incorporators' meeting
Minutes of first board meeting
Consent forms from directors and auditors
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
Registration fee payment receipt
Identification of the applicant (if not an incorporator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order or rejects the application, rectify the identified deficiencies and resubmit. Common issues include incomplete documents, incorrect fees, or discrepancies in the articles. If the rejection is based on substantive legal grounds, seek legal advice to amend the articles or procedures. The applicant may also file an appeal against the rejection within the statutory period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, operating the Home Tax Service (Hometax) electronic portal at hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that establishes a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) in South Korea must register for a Corporate Taxpayer Identification Number (Business Registration Certificate) with the local tax office having jurisdiction over the entity's registered head office address. The incorporation process via the Supreme Court Registry Office automatically notifies the tax authority; the entity must submit the application for business registration (including the corporate application for business registration) to the district tax office (or through Hometax) within the statutory time frame after incorporation. For VAT purposes, the same business registration number serves as the Value-Added Tax registration number, with a unique business type code for VAT. The representative director (foreign or Korean) must provide the corporate seal certificate, articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, and proof of registered address. A foreign non-resident entity without a Korean permanent establishment selling cross-border digital services to Korean consumers may be required to register for simplified VAT registration under the Foreign Business Operator system, using the direct registration process via Hometax with a tax representative if required. For a resident Chusik Hoesa, once the corporate income tax registration is complete, the NTS issues a 10-digit business registration number (e.g., 000-00-00000), which is used for corporate tax, VAT withholding, and customs purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for a domestic Chusik Hoesa; it is automatically treated as a corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax. No check-the-box partnership election exists. However, a foreign entity may be eligible for treaty classification determinations under Korean tax law, and certain hybrid mismatch rules apply under the OECD BEPS framework as implemented in the International Tax Coordination Act. No elective pass-through status is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of South Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory VAT registration; however, a foreign provider of digital services has no threshold and must register effective from the first day of deemed supply of electronic services to Korean consumers. A domestic Chusik Hoesa engaged in business is mandatorily registered irrespective of turnover, but small businesses under the threshold may apply for simplified VAT registration; the general mandatory registration threshold is KRW 80,000,000 in the preceding calendar year (excluding VAT) for suppliers other than new businesses. Newly started businesses must register within 20 days of business commencement regardless of projected turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea mandates electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice / e-Bill) through the NTS Hometax system for all B2B supplies. For B2C transactions, a cash receipt (cash receipt system) must be issued upon request or when the payment amount exceeds KRW 100,000. The e-tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS within the day immediately following the end of the tax period (for monthly VAT filers, by the following month-end in some cases). There is no real-time pre-clearance stamping like Latin America; instead South Korea uses a risk-based real-time electronic tax invoice reporting system, e-Tax Invoice issuance and reporting via the NTS siren system, with the National e-Procurement (KONEPS) integration for government contracts. Digital service foreign providers must register for electronic service supply and issue electronic tax invoices through Hometax if transacting with Korean businesses; for B2C digital services, the foreign provider must file VAT returns quarterly and remit VAT on the gross supply at 10%. Anti-fraud digital stamping is not used; however, the NTS operates a robust e-tax invoice system with mandatory digital signatures and real-time audit data exchange.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated (0% VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods are delivered to a foreign buyer or exported via a customs export declaration. Services and digital content supplied to non-residents are also zero-rated. For a Micro SaaS subscription business, the supply of cloud software and digital content to non-residents (foreign users without a Korean place of business) qualifies for zero rating as 'overseas service exports' under the VAT Act if the place-of-supply rules treat the service as supplied outside Korea or if the consideration is received in foreign currency and the service is actually supplied for use outside Korea. Foreign exchange earned through exports must be repatriated to Korea unless a foreign currency receipt account is maintained with a Korean foreign exchange bank. The zero rating also applies to merchandising sold through overseas app stores, content platforms, and e-commerce when the place of effective use is outside Korea. Documentary substantiation requires a tax invoice for export, an export invoice, a copy of customs clearance (Export Declaration), and proof of payment in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) as filed with Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system
Bill of Lading (AWB / ocean bill / proof of export for intangible services may be substituted by service export invoice and payment evidence)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by the foreign exchange bank or a Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate (FIRC) proving receipt of payment from the foreign purchaser in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the exporter fails to substantiate zero-rated export within the required documentation timeframe or fails to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory deadline, the NTS will reverse the zero rating and assess 10% VAT on the export transaction, plus a 10% additional tax (in addition to the VAT liability) as an uncollected penalty. For a false or fraudulent export zero-rating claim, the importer/exporter may face criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (up to 3 years imprisonment or up to KRW 30,000,000 fine, or both depending on the amount), administrative penalties up to 40% of the evaded VAT, and customs penalties. Moreover, failure to issue and transmit electronic tax invoices can trigger a 2% penalty on the supply value for non-issuance, and a separate penalty of up to 50% of the tax amount for unverified zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the core foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); BOK is the central bank and monetary authority while MOEF regulates foreign exchange business operators and BOK executes statistical monitoring through authorized foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a predominantly liberalised foreign exchange regime under FETA, but the system is not absolutely free in every category. Current account transactions, including software subscriptions, royalties and service fees, are freely convertible and may be remitted once reporting obligations are fulfilled through an authorized foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions are more heavily administered: foreign investment into a Chusik Hoesa must first be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), and the foreign investor must obtain a certificate of foreign investment before the capital escrow can be settled. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may hold earned USD/EUR/JPY in foreign currency accounts, but the claim must be received within six months from the export declaration date and reported for balance-of-payments statistics. Profit remittance, including dividends, is permitted after corporate tax withholding, tax clearance, and submission of FIPA registration proof; banks will require strict differentiation between current and capital flows because loan and dividend paths require different dossiers. In practice, KRW is domestically convertible for business operations and current account remittances, while non-resident access to local KRW funding and speculative FX positions remains carefully ring-fenced by bank position limits and real-demand documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and its subordinate regulations, an exporter must receive export proceeds within six months from the date of the export declaration; this period may be extended for another six months with approval of the Minister of Economy and Finance or the head of an authorized foreign exchange bank in delegated cases. There is no mandatory percentage conversion to KRW: proceeds may be credited to a foreign-currency account, voluntarily surrendered, or used to offset export-related obligations. The receiving foreign exchange bank must report the inward collection to the Bank of Korea as an export receipt for balance-of-payments compilation; failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory period triggers administrative penalties and may be treated as a foreign exchange violation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Reporting Account and Basic KRW Operational Current Account
Basic Operational Currency Account plus Foreign Currency Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account for Paid-in Capital and KRW Operating Current Account
Capital Escrow Account and KRW Account for Subscription Revenue Cleared via Merchant of Record

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-negligible as the sole banking rail. Offshore digital EMIs such as Revolut, Airwallex, and Wise are not authorized foreign exchange banks under FETA and therefore cannot legally open KRW settlement accounts or provide the statutory foreign investment capital escrow, tax clearance, and balance-of-payments reporting that a Korean Chusik Hoesa requires. Local Korean fintech platforms, including Toss Bank and KakaoBank, offer consumer-focused banking and do not act as EU-style EMIs; they may be used only as operational complements if they obtain corporate accounts, but the core treasury and FX compliance must sit with tier-1 domestic banks. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy are viable in the payment flow, but only as merchant-of-record aggregators, not as deposit-taking or FX clearing bodies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the company's domestic representative director, normally a statutory director of the Chusik Hoesa, who must appear in person at the branch for account opening and the real-name financial transaction verification required under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions. Non-resident shareholders and foreign beneficial owners may supply identity documents notarized at a Korean consulate or apostilled, and may be interviewed remotely where a bank's internal policy permits, but Korean banks rarely grant full remote onboarding for newly formed entities with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners. A resident director holding a properly appointed power of attorney is the strongest compliance path; consular proxy is accepted for document certification but not for replacing the mandatory in-branch interview of the statutory representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder opacity and multi-tier corporate parent chain without visible economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified group structure chart; apostilled certificates of incorporation and certificates of good standing for every material shareholder; notarized passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owners; bank reference letters from each shareholder's primary bank; and a three-month source-of-funds statement for the capital to be injected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between consumer subscription revenue collected through Paddle and Lemon Squeezy and the amounts settled to the Korean corporate account, raising disguised-payment or trade-based money-laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant-of-record agreements with the aggregators; panel-level settlement reports and transaction logs; monthly reconciliation mapping each settlement batch to individual customer subscription records; customer invoices, refund and chargeback history; and a statutory declaration from the signatory explaining commissions, taxes, and pooling deductions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Overseas related-party licensing or royalty outflows for the software/IP may create transfer pricing and uncontrolled current-account remittance exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered IP ownership deed; license and SaaS distribution contracts; OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File if group thresholds apply); arm's length royalty benchmarking; withholding tax certificates for each remittance; and board-resolved substance evidence for any cross-border entity receiving royalties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Early-stage Micro-SaaS traction showing rapid recurring revenue but minimal paid-in capital and intercompany loan funding, making the account the target of a loan-back or shell treasury structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or certified management accounts; six months of bank statements; loan agreements with investor lenders; corporate income tax invoices and VAT filings; accounting policy for deferred revenue; and a board-approved cash-flow forecast covering at least twelve months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a foreign investor injecting equity into a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the foreign investor must file a foreign investment report under FIPA at the designated foreign exchange bank and open a foreign investment capital escrow account at the chosen bank. The overseas remittance should be sent through SWIFT MT103 with the investor's account name and reference; the purpose code should be the balance-of-payments code for a foreign direct investment into a domestic company, typically reported as establishment or acquisition of equity in a Korean corporation in the Foreign Exchange Reporting System. After actual inflow, the receiving bank issues a foreign investment registration certificate, and the paid-in capital is verified by the company's external accountant based on the bank deposit certificate and corporate registry. Because the Chusik Hoesa has no minimum capital requirement, the injection amount can be tailored to the operating plan but must be consistent with the FIPA report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Consumer subscriptions are settled through Paddle or Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record; the aggregators collect presentation fees and applicable taxes and remit net proceeds in USD/EUR/GBP to the Korean entity's foreign-currency account. The bank converts those receipts to KRW using booked FX rates. For B2B and infrastructure payments, the main clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for service fees, dividends, and royalties; commercial import documentary letters of credit for hardware or cloud services purchased from vendors; and documentary collection for high-value transactions where an LC is not cost-effective. Every outbound payment must be accompanied by an invoice, contract, and underlying FX purpose code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward exchange contracts with an authorized foreign exchange bank, provided the entity demonstrates a genuine underlying trade or investment exposure and the contract tenor generally does not exceed one year without documented renewal.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for true trade hedge end users and within the bank's position limits established under FETA; Korean domestic corporate hedgers typically migrate to onshore forwards rather than NDFs because onshore forwards are fully legal and settle in KRW, while offshore NDFs carry additional reporting burdens.

Cross-currency swaps for long-term foreign-currency loan-to-KRW conversion are allowed where the swap is supported by actual non-resident borrowing and the bank approves the transaction as an enterprise hedge, not speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and payment for the prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; by the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end for other fiscal years; externally audited companies may use the statutory extension to April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a 20% non-declaration penalty on the unreported or underreported tax, a 10% underpayment penalty, and statutory late-payment interest calculated on each day of delay. Persistent non-filing permits the NTS to seize assets, proceed with forced collection, close the business place, and, where appropriate, request a court to order dissolution; there is no automatic administrative strike-off for a Chusik Hoesa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office of the metropolitan city, province, si, or gun where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as national corporate tax; by March 31 for calendar-year entities, with an extension to April 30 for externally audited companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent local tax attracts local-tax negligence penalties and daily delinquency interest under the Local Tax Act; continued non-payment may result in demand letters, property seizure, public auction of assets, and suspension of business-related local tax certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First-half preliminary VAT return for January 1 to June 30 is due July 25; second-half final VAT return for July 1 to December 31 is due January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underreporting triggers a 20% negligent-payment penalty plus statutory daily late-payment interest; repeated or serious VAT non-compliance can lead to tax offense investigations, business premises closure, and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of shareholders and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed centrally; recorded in the company minute book at the registered office and made available for inspection by shareholders, NTS, and court authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual ordinary general meeting must be convened within three months after the close of each fiscal year, which for a calendar-year company means by March 31, unless unavoidable circumstances justify a postponement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the annual meeting within the statutory window may be subject to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act; financial statements cannot be validly approved, director discharge may be precluded, and continuous governance default may support involuntary judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements when the statutory audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants through the external audit reporting system; tax-related copies filed with the National Tax Service where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The external auditor must be engaged within four months after the start of the fiscal year; audited financial statements must be submitted to the FSS within two weeks after shareholder approval and before the final corporate tax filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the audit report is punishable by criminal fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the company may be treated as non-compliant for financial reporting and tax purposes and may face additional regulatory sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise annual status report where a foreign investor holds an FDI-qualifying stake of 10% or more
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through delegated reception by Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or a designated foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year, which for calendar-year companies is by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or materially late filing of the annual foreign direct investment report may trigger administrative fines and can impair foreign-investment tax incentives or future exchange-control approvals; it does not automatically dissolve the Korean entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: On-site statutory corporate register inspection and preservation review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; statutory registers and minute books are kept at the registered office and must be presented to shareholders, creditors, NTS, and the court upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; annual internal verification should be completed immediately before the annual shareholders meeting and before the corporate tax filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the register of shareholders, register of directors, pledge register, and minute books subjects responsible officers to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act; false or negligent register entries may create civil liability and adverse evidentiary presumptions against the company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a private Chusik Hoesa is compulsorily required to obtain an independent certified CPA audit if it is listed; if it is a financial institution or designated public-interest entity; or if its total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end reach the statutory threshold, currently generally KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million at an illustrative exchange rate of 1,330 KRW/USD). Additional quantitative triggers may apply under the statute on the basis of annual revenue, total liabilities, and employee headcount for specified categories. A consumer micro-SaaS company with minimal assets and no employees is generally below the compulsory audit threshold unless it satisfies a separate statutory designation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean IFRS (K-IFRS) is mandatory for listed companies, financial institutions, and designated public-interest entities. Non-listed companies that are subject to external audit may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) established by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, or may elect K-IFRS consistently. Smaller non-audited companies may prepare financial statements under K-GAAP or SME accounting standards acceptable for corporate tax and creditor purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For an unlisted Chusik Hoesa, South Korea does not impose a recurring annual public UBO affirmation form to the Companies Registry. The company must maintain an accurate shareholder register and update it promptly upon any share transfer, pledge, or statutory corporate change; a transferee acquires rights against the company only when entered in the shareholder register. Where a transfer creates a reportable foreign direct investment of 10% or more voting ownership, or crosses disclosure thresholds under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, a report must be made to the relevant financial or trade authority within 30 days of the triggering event. Financial institutions performing AML/KYC reviews may require the company to confirm its ultimate beneficial owners on an ongoing basis, and material ownership changes should be communicated to affected counterparties as soon as commercially practicable and no later than 30 days after the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including shareholder ledger and stock transfer records)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (pledges and security interests over shares)
Minute Book (shareholder resolutions and board resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 12,000 per year when a statutory audit is triggered; not applicable when the company is below the compulsory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% maximum aggregate statutory rate (22% national corporate income tax on taxable income above KRW 20 billion plus 10% local income tax surtax, with progressive lower rates of 10% for the first KRW 200 million and 20% for the next KRW 19.8 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Venture company 50% corporate income tax reduction for five years if registered under Korean venture enterprise statutes and meeting domestic business requirements; R&D tax credit up to 30% for qualifying software research and development expenses; no patent box regime for SaaS products; small and medium enterprise special tax rates applicable to micro-SaaS.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Report (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서, Form 406-500) filed electronically via the National Tax Service Home Tax System (HTS / e-Tax).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; one interim prepayment (중간예납) per fiscal year for corporations with prior-year corporate tax liability exceeding KRW 10 million (due within two months after the first six-month period of the fiscal year).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end, e.g., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end; automatically extended to six months (e.g., June 30) when a licensed tax agent preparer is engaged or when overseas branches are present.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all worldwide gross revenue from micro-SaaS subscription fees, software license fees, and in-app purchases, including revenue collected via Paddle or Lemon Squeezy from foreign customers. Because the Korean company is a resident entity, foreign customer revenue is Korea-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not insert income in this box, but the Korean company must separately disclose related-party revenue in attached schedules to allow transfer pricing inspection. If revenue is routed through an offshore payment entity, ensure the Korean entity has the economic substance to be treated as the true seller.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include direct costs such as cloud hosting fees, payment processing charges, software maintenance, and amortization of internally developed software. Capitalize software development costs and amortize over a conservative useful life (e.g., five years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to overseas related parties for cloud infrastructure, platform services, or licensing must be at arm's length and supported by contemporaneous functional and comparability analysis. Royalties or service fees paid to a foreign shell company without substance will be disallowed and trigger withholding tax and transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated as Box 1 minus Box 2. Maintain reconciliation with the audited financial statements; no separate non-resident reporting line is needed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consistent foreign exchange rates on transaction dates or accrual rates for multi-currency sales; any unrealized FX gains or losses are recognized in subsequent boxes. Ensure that intercompany revenue offsets do not distort gross profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include marketing, affiliate commissions, employee salaries, office rent, legal and professional fees, and other operating expenses. Deductibility is subject to statutory caps, e.g., entertainment expense limits and political contribution restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border advertising or user-acquisition payments to foreign platforms may be subject to Korean VAT and withholding tax if the services are rendered in Korea or connected to a Korean permanent establishment. For digital marketing from abroad, review the applicable DTA business profits article to determine whether Korean source services income arises; properly file a non-resident withholding return when necessary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report interest income, dividends received from foreign affiliates, FX gains/losses, and other non-operating items. Foreign dividend income must be included in Korean taxable income, with entitlement to a foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from a foreign subsidiary are not automatically exempt under a DTA; the Korean company must include them and claim an indirect foreign tax credit for underlying corporate taxes paid if the treaty provides for it (e.g., shareholding of at least 10% for certain treaties). Avoid double taxation by filing Form to claim foreign tax credit attached to the corporate return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Taxable Base, Loss Carryforward and Adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile book income to taxable income: add non-deductible expenses, subtract tax-exempt income, apply transfer pricing adjustments, and deduct net operating loss carryforwards (statutory carryforward of 10 years for most corporations, 15 years for certain SMEs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from a foreign permanent establishment may not be used to offset Korean income if the PE is recognized under a DTA and chooses the foreign tax credit regime. Deficiency of deductions must be properly substantiated with Korean tax adjustment schedules; ignore loss deductions from aggressive tax-haven structures to avoid government reassessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Calculated Tax and Net Tax Payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the national corporate income tax at progressive rates (10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% above KRW 20 billion). Add 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax. Deduct interim prepayments, withholding tax credits, tax credits, and foreign tax credits. The final balance is the net payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any foreign income tax withheld by a foreign jurisdiction should be claimed here as a foreign tax credit, limited to the Korean corporate tax attributable to that income. The non-resident shareholders' tax consequences arise only upon distributions, not in this box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual corporate income tax return results in a surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax for late filing; failure to remit the computed tax triggers an additional 20% underreporting penalty for non-negligent omissions and 40% for fraudulent understatement, plus an overdue interest surcharge of approximately 0.025% per day (annual 9.125%). For omission of revenue records, a gross-income penalty of 0.5% per day (capped at 36.5% of the omitted revenue) may also apply. Criminal prosecution is available under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 100 million for aggravated fraudulent evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on cash dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (20% national income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Korean paying company before remittance: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's own tax authority; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration on the official NTS form for reduced treaty tax (Form “Application for Income Exemption or Reduction under a Tax Treaty”) stating that the shareholder is the ultimate beneficial owner of the dividend/interest/royalty income and has no Korean PE to which the income is effectively connected; (3) evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period (e.g., holding at least 10% of shares for 365 days to qualify for certain 5%-10% treaty dividend rates); (4) if the full statutory rate was withheld, a refund claim must be filed with the National Tax Service within the statutory claim period (generally 2 years from the filing deadline) attaching the TRC and a fresh certificate of beneficial ownership. DTA relief will be denied if the principal purpose of the structure is to obtain treaty benefits, and the NTS may require supplementary proof of economic substance, including local employees, office premises, and actual decision-making functions of the shareholder during the holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT is 22% (20% plus 2% local surcharge) for interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Under Korea's tax treaties, rates are commonly reduced: interest 10%-15%, royalties 10%-15% depending on the jurisdiction. For software licenses (SaaS/Cloud), most DTAs apply a 10% rate to royalty income if the beneficial owner is the recipient. Korean thin capitalization rules further deny interest deductions on loans from controlling foreign shareholders exceeding a 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio (6:1 for financial institutions).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 8 million) for aggregate international related-party transactions in a fiscal year, which triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; CbCR filing threshold is KRW 1 trillion consolidated group revenue for the ultimate parent.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not have an Economic Substance Regulation similar to the UAE, but the NTS applies the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 14 of the Basic Act for National Tax and the OECD BEPS minimum standards. For a Korean micro-SaaS company, core income-generating activities (CIGA) include software development, server maintenance, data security, customer support, and revenue collection. The Korean entity must have real employees, office facilities, and decision-making authority over those activities. A foreign holding company that merely licenses IP into Korea without any substance will be disregarded for treaty relief and profits will be recharacterized as Korean-source through a Korean PE or a sham transaction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Fraudulent Revenue Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately hiding micro-SaaS subscription revenue earned from foreign customers via online payment gateways (Paddle, Lemon Squeezy) by diverting the payments to a director's personal offshore bank account or failing to book invoiced sales in the Korean corporate ledger.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (Articles 3 and 8) and the Corporate Tax Act. The NTS will impose a 40% surcharge on the understated tax, plus a 20% non-filing surcharge and daily overdue interest of 0.025% (annual 9.125%). Fraudulent evasion exceeding material thresholds is a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to KRW 100 million, or both.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced under Article 13 of the Basic Act for National Tax when the director acts as the de facto taxpayer or uses the company solely as a vehicle for tax avoidance. The director is personally liable for the evaded tax, penalties, and interest. The director's assets may be subject to seizure, and the NTS may impose a travel ban (blacklisting) preventing departure from Korea if unpaid tax exceeds KRW 200 million. Criminal conviction leads to imprisonment and a permanent criminal record.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Sham Intercompany Services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a non-arm's length arrangement with a related foreign company in a low-tax jurisdiction (e.g., paying excessive SaaS platform management fees, IP royalties, or cloud infrastructure fees to an entity with no actual employees, assets, or function, thereby artificially shifting Korean profits abroad).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA), the NTS adjusts related-party transactions to the arm's length price and imposes a 20% unjustified-return penalty on the underpaid corporate tax, plus overdue interest. Failure to submit a Local/Master File when the threshold is met carries an additional 30% documentation-related surcharge and administrative fines up to KRW 20 million. The transaction may be recharacterized and the foreign entity ignored.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who signs false contracts, creates phantom invoices, or issues certificates supporting a sham intercompany arrangement is jointly and severally liable for the additional corporate tax, penalties, and interest. Criminal liability under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for preparing false tax invoices carries imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to KRW 50 million. Directors may also be subjected to departure restraint (travel ban) and civil asset claims for breach of fiduciary duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Treaty Relief Claim and Beneficial Ownership Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a conduit company in a treaty jurisdiction (e.g., Singapore, Hong Kong, or the Netherlands) with no office, staff, or real decision-making, to hold shares or receive dividends/royalties from the Korean micro-SaaS company only for the purpose of gaining the reduced DTA withholding rate, while the ultimate beneficial owner resides in a non-treaty tax haven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will deny the treaty benefit under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) or Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clause of the DTA, and under the domestic General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Article 14 of the Basic Act for National Tax). The Korean payer is assessed the differential withholding tax (22% statutory minus the claimed treaty rate), plus a 40% penalty for willful misrepresentation, and interest. Refund claims made by the conduit are denied with additional penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify or knowingly approve a fraudulent beneficial ownership application are personally liable for the under-withheld tax, as they have breached their statutory duty to verify the recipient's substance. Under Article 11 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, aiding and abetting a tax evasion scheme is punishable by up to 2 years' imprisonment and fines. The NTS may attach the director's personal bank accounts, real estate, and vehicles, and may impose a travel ban on all directors and the registered agent.
